summary: Title V applies to major sources and certain listed source categories. EPA states that a major source has actual or potential emissions at or above 100 tons/year for an air pollutant by default, with lower nonattainment thresholds for the nonattainment pollutant, and 10 tons/year for a single HAP or 25 tons/year combined HAPs. The Clean Air Act likewise makes it unlawful to operate a major source or other specified source subject to Title V except in compliance with a Title V permit, and defines a major stationary source generally as one that emits or has the potential to emit 100 tons/year or more of any air pollutant. California’s CARB confirms Title V is implemented through California air districts and that applications are generally required for any CAA “major source,” affected acid-rain source, Section 129 solid-waste incinerator, or EPA-designated category. For the project facts supplied—storage of 60 gallons of flammable solvent at a coating shop with a coating/paint operation—there is no location/air district, attainment classification, solvent composition/VOC-HAP content, usage/emission rate, or facility potential-to-emit calculation. Therefore Title V applicability is indeterminate. Based only on the stated change (storage of 60 gallons), the record does not establish that the facility meets Title V major-source thresholds or another listed Title V category.
title: H-AIR-TITLE-V — Title V operating permit applicability cannot be determined from the provided facts; the described solvent storage alone is not evidence of a major source
